# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

• **Audit what you're actually selling right now** — Have each coach list every service/package they've ever sold or discussed. You'll find inconsistencies (different prices, inclusions, messaging). This is your raw material. Takes 2 hours max with a quick team call.

• **Price anchoring move** — Start with your highest-value offering (likely 1-on-1 coaching). Lock that price first, then work backwards. Your group classes and memberships should feel cheaper *relative to that anchor*, making them obvious value plays. Test pricing on 5-10 existing members before finalizing.

• **Create two separate documents** (not one confusing master list):
  - **Coach version**: What each service entails, time required, any prep/follow-up, how to upsell/cross-sell naturally
  - **Member version**: Clean, benefit-focused (not feature-dumping). Include "this is for you if..." language for each tier

• **Make it a sales tool, not decoration** — Your coaches should be able to reference it mid-conversation. Laminate cards or pin it in the coaching area. If coaches aren't naturally referencing it within 2 weeks, you'll know it's missing something they actually need.

• **Lock it for 90 days minimum** — Changing prices/offerings constantly erodes trust. Commit to the menu, track what sells, *then* iterate. This discipline matters more than perfection now.

What's your current pricing variance like across coaches?

# THE FORGE — FRACTIONAL CFO ASSESSMENT

## REVENUE — URGENT ATTENTION NEEDED

• **Membership revenue collapsed in August (£16,160 vs £19,764 in July; -18%)**. Active members jumped to 155 in August (+19 from July) but Rev/member plummeted to £104 from £145 — you're onboarding at a lower price point or losing high-value tier subscribers. **Action:** audit your pricing tiers in TeamUp now. Are new members entering at intro/trial rates? Lock in 3-month commitment at full price (typically £35–50/month for women's premium gyms in Belfast); run a survey on Aug churn (5.6%) to find if it's price-sensitive or service-related.

• **Churn spiked to 12.8% in May** — red flag. Last 3 months (June–Aug) average 5.7%, which is healthier but still high for a dedicated members' gym (industry benchmark ~3–4%). **Action:** implement a churn intervention: automated email at day 60 of membership lapse, 1-to-1 check-in call for members inactive 4+ weeks, loyalty discount (10% off 3-month renewal) for at-risk cohorts.

• **Rev/member has eroded**: Feb £131 → Aug £104 (-20%). This is your biggest profit leak. **Action:** (1) Kill or raise any introductory pricing under £25/month; (2) create a premium tier (classes + personal training credits, nutrition guides) at £65–75/month, target existing high-attendance members; (3) launch class bundles (10 × unlimited classes = £80, valid 60 days) to convert casual drop-ins into committed payers.

---

## EXPENSES — CASH BURN IN MONTHS WITHOUT RELOCATION

• **Aug cash burn of -£5,335 is the real concern** (excluding April relocation). Your operating cash is negative despite £16.1k revenue. **Action:** pull full P&L for Aug now — break down payroll, rent, utilities, supplies by line. Typical gym cost structure should be 55–65% payroll, 15–20% rent/facilities, 10–15% other. If you're running over that, identify which line. Suspect August had extra staffing or one-off costs post-relocation; if recurring, you need to cut 1 FTE or renegotiate supplier contracts.

• **Net cash trend is volatile**: Feb +£3.6k, March -£5.3k, May +£3.6k
